etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English banishen, from Old French baniss-, extended stem of banir (“to proclaim, ban, banish”), from Latin banniō (“to summon, ban, excommunicate, etc.”), from Frankish *bannijan (“to summon, to banish”), from Proto-Germanic *bannaną (“to proclaim, order, summon, ban”, root also of Old English bannan (“to summon”), whence Modern English ban), from a Proto-Indo-European root *bʰeh₂- (“to speak/say”). Compare French bannir, Portuguese banir, Italian bandire.
senses: (transitive) To send (someone) away and forbid them from returning.
(transitive) To expel, especially from the mind.
